$comment: D-CSUBSET-CONST-EVAL-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS + D-CSUBSET-CHAR-HIGHBYTE-ICE-SIGNEDNESS: the COMPILE-TIME witness for plain `char`'s declared signedness. The sibling examples/c/char_signedness pins the RUNTIME half only, and that is exactly how this defect survived: the runtime tier was the ONE consumer that read the declaration, so a green runtime witness proved nothing about the four compile-time tiers beside it. Read main.c for the bit weights; each exit code below is 150 + one weighted bit per tier, so a regression in a single tier moves the number by a distinct amount rather than being absorbed by its siblings. ★ THE VALUES ARE DERIVED FROM THE ONE `charIsUnsigned` DECLARATION AND ARE NOT TWO INDEPENDENT HAND-WRITTEN NUMBERS: every leg where the target configuration resolves plain `char` to SIGNED reads 181 (all five bits set), and the ONE leg it resolves to UNSIGNED reads 151 (only the target-independent WIDTH bit set, because on an unsigned-`char` leg `'\xff' < 0` is genuinely false). The signed set is x86_64 under every object format plus arm64 x macho (Apple's platform ABI fixes `char` SIGNED); the unsigned set is arm64 x elf alone, which is the only unsigned-`char` leg DSS ships. ⚠⚠ THE arm64 x elf ROW IS NOT A COPY OF THE OTHERS AND MUST NEVER BE FLIPPED TO 181 — on that leg the buggy answer and the correct answer to `'\xff' < 0` COINCIDE, which is precisely why no test on that leg could ever have seen the defect. Its value is what proves the fix is CONFIG-DRIVEN rather than a hard-coded flip: make the compiler assume signed everywhere and this row silently reads 181. Conversely its WIDTH bit is what keeps the row non-vacuous at all, because `(char)300 == 44` holds under BOTH signedness readings and was MEASURED WRONG on BOTH legs at b1f31420. ✔MEASURED at b1f31420, each reference probed SEPARATELY with a control matching its own target: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (native x86_64-linux) both answer 42 to `('\xff' < 0) ? 42 : 45` in the runtime, ICE and `#if` forms while DSS answered 42 / 45 / 45; aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 under qemu-aarch64 answers 45 to all three (the unsigned leg) while DSS answered 45 / 45 / 45 — right for the wrong reason; and on the CAST forms aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc answers 45 to `((char)200 == -56) ? 42 : 45` where DSS answered 42, the mirror-image error. MSVC 19.51 (`cl.exe /nologo /c /std:c17`) accepts a `typedef char x[('\xff' < 0) ? 1 : -1]` plus the `#if` and `(char)200 == -56 && (char)300 == 44` arms at rc 0, with a deliberately known-FALSE control arm in the same file that errors C2118 — so the clean rc is not vacuous. Unanimous against the pre-fix DSS in every direction. ★ RUNNABILITY: each row runs only where its `runOn` admits it; the rows the host cannot execute are still COMPILED, and their expectations rest on the reference measurements above plus the single target declaration.

targets.$comment: ★ THE ONE UNSIGNED-`char` LEG DSS SHIPS, AND THE ONLY ROW HERE THAT IS NOT 181. `'\xff' < 0` is genuinely FALSE on aarch64-linux-gnu, so the four target-keyed bits (RUNTIME 16, ICE 8, PREPROCESSOR 4, STATIC-INIT 2) are all 0 and only the target-INDEPENDENT WIDTH bit is set: 150 + 1 = 151. Two distinct failure readings, and they mean opposite things. If this row reads 181, the compiler stopped consulting the declaration and is assuming signed everywhere — the fix was hard-coded, not config-driven. If it reads 150, the WIDTH bit went out, i.e. plain `char` is being modelled wider than eight bits again; that is the same defect that MEASURED `static int g = (char)300; g == 44` as FALSE in DSS on BOTH legs at b1f31420 while gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 all answer TRUE. ⚠ Do NOT 'fix' a disagreement here by flipping this row toward its siblings: this row and the arm64 x macho row below are ONE CPU on TWO platforms and are SUPPOSED to differ, for the same reason the two arm64 rows of examples/c/char_signedness are supposed to differ. If they ever read the same number this example has stopped testing the thing it exists to test.

★ SIGNED, LIKE THE x86_64 ROWS AND UNLIKE ITS OWN CPU'S elf ROW ABOVE. Apple's arm64 platform ABI fixes plain `char` SIGNED, so all five bits are set and this row reads 181. It is a SECOND non-vacuous leg for the signedness half: C 6.2.5p15 leaves the choice to the platform, so the same processor answers differently under two object formats, and this row is where a fix that keyed off the ARCHITECTURE instead of the (architecture x object-format) pair would show up as 151.
